stories.title: A woman passes a year with a kidney from a gene-edited pig
stories.summary: Molly Falco, 58, has lived a year with a kidney from a gene-edited pig at Mass General Brigham, the longest any known recipient has, and is off dialysis. It's one patient and still experimental; her doctor hopes an approved option could come in about five years if a trial next year goes well.

stories.title: OpenAI's chief scientist proposes shared limits on AI development, measured by 'perplexity'
stories.summary: Jakub Pachocki published OpenAI's internal perplexity scores (how well a model predicts text) and proposed that AI labs agree on limits they won't cross until they can monitor AI behaviour better. It's one company's proposal and its own measurements, not an agreement.

predictions.note: OpenAI's chief scientist proposed shared limits labs would not cross until AI monitoring reaches a set milestone; a proposal from one company, not a pause.
He called for shared norms to evaluate new models and red-team their safety cases by first use; one company's proposal, not a requirement.

stories.title: Two mathematicians claim an AI-aided proof that fluid equations can blow up on their own
stories.summary: Anthropic's Levent Alpöge and NYU's Tristan Buckmaster posted an AI-aided proof that the Navier-Stokes equations for fluid flow can blow up with no outside push, closing a loophole in OpenAI's September proof of the $1M prize problem. It's an unchecked claim; its certificate isn't out yet.
stories.evidence: Claimed proof; not yet checked or peer reviewed

predictions.note: An NYU mathematician and an Anthropic mathematician posted an AI-aided proof that fluid equations blow up unaided; one unchecked result, not a measured speedup.

stories.title: A start-up says its AI agents designed a new processor from scratch
stories.summary: Architect Labs says AI agents designed Frostbite, from its instruction set to its layout, with 4.59 times the performance per watt of a conventional core across 25 workloads. It's the company's own pre-silicon simulation, against an unnamed core; no chip exists yet.

predictions.note: AI agents doing a chip's architecture, design and layout is the forecast's work, but this is one start-up's own pre-silicon claim.

stories.title: OpenAI's new test of AI drug-design reasoning: its best model earns 84.5%
stories.summary: MedChemBench tests AI on 99 medicinal-chemistry problems drawn from 117 papers and patents. OpenAI's best model, GPT-6.2 Astra, earned 84.5% of the credit. It's the company's own test of its own models, a step towards AI that helps chemists choose which molecules to make.
stories.evidence: Company benchmark of its own models

stories.title: Why the left brain runs the right body: a theory points to ancient fish eyes
stories.summary: University of Minnesota neuroscientists propose that the brain's crossed wiring began in vision, in jawless fish over 500 million years ago, with touch and pain pathways following its lead. It's a theory built from existing studies in Frontiers in Neuroanatomy, with no new experiments.

stories.title: Britons conceived under sugar rationing test biologically younger in their 50s
stories.summary: Among 54,201 UK Biobank adults, those conceived under Britain's sugar rationing, which ended in 1953, had a blood-test biological age up to about five months lower in their 50s, and 22% less chronic kidney disease. It's an observational natural experiment, a link rather than proof.

stories.title: With nutrients matched, an ultraprocessed meal still brought a bigger insulin surge
stories.summary: In a Virginia Tech trial, 32 adults ate two ~300-calorie meals matched within 1.6% on a dozen nutrition measures. Blood sugar was similar, but insulin ran higher from 40 to 120 minutes after the ultraprocessed meal. A small trial of single meals in healthy young adults.

stories.title: In mice, a Berkeley compound burned fat but spared muscle
stories.summary: UC Berkeley's compound TOFA blocks fat-making and switches on fat-burning genes. In obese mice it raised energy use by up to 18% and cut fat without a significant loss of muscle, and it boosted GLP-1 drugs. It hasn't been tested in people.

stories.title: Adding core exercises helped people with knee arthritis more than knee exercises alone
stories.summary: In a randomised trial in India, 100 people aged 40-80 with mild to moderate knee osteoarthritis did 12 weeks of rehab; adding core work such as planks and glute bridges improved function, pain on movement and quality of life more. A small trial in one country.

stories.title: Therapists who tried fast breathing reported psychedelic-like bliss
stories.summary: In Berlin, 48 psychiatrists and psychotherapists tried 30 minutes of fast, continuous breathing; their bliss and unity scores looked similar to moderate psychedelic doses in other studies. A small exploratory study with no control group: it shows their impressions, not that it treats anything.

stories.title: Low-dose THC made people feel high but didn't ease a stressful memory
stories.summary: In a University of Chicago lab study of 36 healthy adults, low oral doses of THC made people feel high but didn't ease their distress when reminded of a stressful task, then or a week later. A small study in healthy volunteers, not people with PTSD.

stories.title: ChatGPT's Mandarin versions of mental-health checklists changed from user to user
stories.summary: A University of Canterbury study had ChatGPT translate two mental-health screening scales into Mandarin for New Zealand. One well-crafted prompt worked better, but colleagues running the same prompt got different wording, and screening tools need to work the same way every time.

stories.title: US banks crack down on AI agents logging into customers' accounts
stories.summary: WIRED reports Wells Fargo's new terms say using an AI agent is at your own risk, and JPMorgan Chase bans third-party agents that log in with your password; Bank of America, Citibank and PNC have also warned customers. A brake on handing everyday money tasks to AI agents, for now.

stories.title: Part of the Milky Way's Norma arm may not be a spiral arm at all
stories.summary: University of Sydney astronomer Hillary Davis found that stars form along a shock front of the Milky Way's central bar, which is unusual among nearby galaxies, so at least part of the Norma spiral arm may not be an arm. Published in Nature Astronomy, comparing simulations with observations.

sources.outlet: University of Sydney via Mirage News

stories.title: A physicist built a mock black hole from logic gates, then made it leak
stories.summary: Keio University's Antonino Flachi built an analogue black hole out of logic gates, about 604 million bits, where ripples get trapped at a horizon; when he poked it, it leaked. A preprint, not yet peer reviewed, and a model in digital logic rather than a real black hole.

stories.title: A reusable space factory for growing drug crystals aims to fly by 2030
stories.summary: Luxembourg's Space Cargo Unlimited showed a full-size model of REV1, a reusable space factory built to bring a tonne of cargo home and fly about 20 times, for things like drug crystals that grow more evenly in orbit. A company plan: it's targeting flight readiness in 2030.
